CLAIM 1, Gauss law (exact; A c1, B c01). [H,G_v] = -i eta_v h sum Y_e with residual 0; every non-flip owner commutes with G_v (carrier, Bind, n_e T_e hop, admission, both feedbacks, cells, Hcell, HA), residual 0.0. Dipole q4 multigraph (dense dim 2304): G_a+G_b = 0, G P2 = 0 (dim P2 = 864). At h=0, spec G_a = {-2..2}, so G is a conserved label, not an imposed constraint. Doubled 4-ring q4 (dim 5,308,416), checked exhaustively: 16 hops (663,552 elements each), 4 Bind (2,654,208), 8 admission (884,736), max|dG| = 0; 18 ice words and 373,248 ice states all have G = 0. Region Gauss law (sum G over a region = boundary flux of n_e - 1/2) is exact on K44 for all 65536 words. Birth: dipole all-cut gives a Born graph with 2 balanced components and a connected union; on 864 images G_new(retained) = G_old, G_star = 0, T injective; ring 0-1/2-3 cut gives the same on 1,990,656 images.

CLAIM 2, Record vertex (exact; A c2, B c01/c07). d q = 2q + eta G q on every state (the eta-free d = 2+G fails on B sites, and the packet's form is correct). Diagonal rewrite sum_v[Ud s^2 + mu_v s] + const, with mu_v = Delta/2 + 2Ud(2-d*) + lamJ p - lamR q, is exact in fractions: 256x256 words (A) and 400 random words (B). D_e = 2Ud + sigma(mu_u+mu_v) holds in all 36,864 ice-flip cases. Diagonal energy is identical on all 18 ice words, so there is no bare polarization vertex. Two-level q_low = (1 - a/sqrt(a^2+4g^2))/2 and dq/dd = 2g^2 lamR/(a^2+4g^2)^{3/2} (lamR=1/8): (3,2) 1/5, 1/125; (-3,2) 4/5, 1/125; (5,6) 4/13, 9/2197; (8,3) 1/10, 9/4000; (5/2,3) 4/13, 18/2197. Upper branch has the opposite sign; dense numeric 0.0079999999958.

Ring-sign cohomology (A c5; periodic diamond, 64 sites, 128 links, 128 hexagons). Flipping the sign on the 12 hexagons through v is NOT a Z2 coboundary. Flipping the 6 hexagons through one link is a coboundary, and so is flipping all hexagons.

Verdict basis: claims (1)-(4) were not refuted as operator identities, sum rules or Gaussian-toy relations. Every exact check held. The corrections below concern interpretation, an incomplete vertex census, binding, and missed channels.
problems: P1 (substantive; §3, §5, §6): the direct Record vertex couples to a sublattice-staggered quantity, not to div E. -lamR eta_v G_v q_v = -lamR s_v q_v with s = d-2 = eta G. Every native owner depends on d_v and n_e and never on eta. Any A<->B automorphism (C', e.g. diamond inversion) maps G -> -G, so E is axial under C'. In a C'-symmetric, unpolarized background no scalar Record vertex can be linear in rho_G or E, by any channel. Consequences: (i) the per-site response c eta_v rho_ind(r_v) is a staggered Yukawa. (ii) Its exterior shell-averaged scalar part has zero Yukawa-pole residue at O(Q_G): on the imaginary-k pole f is real, so 4+m-f* = 0. Diamond smoothed shells give |sum s/sum G| <= 2.5e-5 for R >= 9 (Kchi=0.2) and <= 2.1e-4 (Kchi=1), with sum|s| = |sum G|. (iii) What remains is an xyz-octupole Yukawa (projection 6.5e-5, 25x the residual monopole) plus a source-local total sum s = 2zQ/(2z+Kchi): 8Q/(8+Kchi) on q4 diamond (0.975610 and 8/9 verified), 4Q/(4+Kchi) on a chain. This total is the staggered Fourier component (L eta = 2z eta), not a tail. (iv) For C'-symmetric probes the sublattice sum is exactly zero: ideal 4-species gas 0 for any mu (nonzero once mu_A != mu_B, -0.0809). For K44 at h=0.35, mu=0.3, ds_A_i = -ds_B_i with pair sums <= 2.6e-12, against -0.354 for the A-only control. (v) Carriers bind charge eta_site, so C'-symmetric matter has zero mean G and no coherent monopole. The incoherent <E^2> = N/(16 pi^2 r^4) (sampled ratio 1.05). Reconciliation of the two reviewers: 'linear shell-averaged response is exactly zero' holds for the effective scalar-vertex coefficient and for C'-symmetric probes. Around a lattice point source, the exterior Yukawa residue vanishes but the source-local total does not.

P2 (substantive; §2): the binding diagnostic omits the leading native mechanism and can get the sign wrong. Hopping is -t n_e T_e, so in ice a carrier moves only on the occupied 2-regular subgraph (loops). s=+1 is a T-junction. Exact at g=0 with infinite legs: it binds iff lamJ < |t|, with x = (lamJ+sqrt(lamJ^2+8t^2))/(4t) and B+ = t(x+1/x) - 2t. Values: 0.121320t = (3/sqrt2-2)t at lamJ=0, 0.067091t at lamJ=1/4. s=-1 is a chain end: it binds iff lamJ > |t|, with B- = (lamJ-t)^2/lamJ (0.1667t at lamJ=1.5t). B's ED (L=70) matches to 1e-10 and the merge ED (L=400) to 1e-14. The neutral single-flip pair (H-junction) binds more strongly than a single charge: (sqrt5-2)t = 0.236068t at lamJ=0 and 0.136001t at lamJ=1/4. With Bind in a written background (<= 1 erased Record), s=+1 binding survives: 0.0633, 0.0486, 0.0366, 0.0407 (c02 parameter sets). The packet's lamJ-only bias favours s=-1. At the P45 tuple (lamJ=1/4) with |t| > 1/4, the bound defect is s=+1. The diagonal-only statement (a carrier lowers the sigma=-1 pair cost by lamJ, which binds nothing at Ud=100, lamJ=1/4) is true but incomplete. Every carrier+defect object costs about 2U_d (200 at the tuple), so it is an excitation, not ground-state background.

P3 (substantive; §4 incomplete and mis-ordered). (a) Missing native O(h^2) pair-word vertex: 2h^2 Delta2b sum_e q_u q_v E_e, plus q-p and p-p analogs. It couples adjacent Record pair words linearly to divergence-free polarization, at lower order than the h^6 ring vertex. Definitions: Delta2b = b(z-2lamR) - 2b(z-lamR) + b(z), b(z) = [1/(2Ud+z) - 1/(2Ud-z)]/2 = -z/(4Ud^2-z^2), z = Delta + 4Ud(2-d*). Exact 2Delta2b: -8/5355 (Ud=1, Delta=1/4, d*=2, lamR=1/8); +8/5355 (Delta=0); -8/546132266667 (Ud=100, Delta=1/4); +8/546132266667 (Ud=100, Delta=0); identically 0 at z = lamR because b is odd. Leading term: Delta2b = -3 lamR^2 (z-lamR)/(8Ud^4) + higher, so O(h^2 lamR^3/Ud^4) at z=0. Doubled-ring probe: the single-site coefficient is 128/5355 for both m=2 and m=0, and 2/255 for an erasure from all-written. The adjacent pair gives -1/105 vs -1/153, difference -16/5355 = 4 Delta2b. ED h^2 coefficients agree with -sum 1/D_e to 4e-9. §3's single-site and single-erasure blindness stands; pair erasures are not blind. (b) Ring-vertex order count: at delta=0 the single-site Record ring vertex is EVEN in lamR, because hexagon reflection maps the word to its complement. dc6/dmu_v = 0 and d^2c6/dmu_v^2 = 165/16 at U=1; controls c6 = 63/8 and 2504/81 are reproduced. At the tuple (lamR/U = 1/800), Delta c6/c6 = 1.023e-6 (one written on blank) and 1.432e-6 (one blank on written). The linear term is lamR C mu0 with C = 99/8. The packet's O(lamR h^6/D^6) should read O(lamR max(lamR,|delta|) h^6/D^7).

P4 (scope; §5, §6): Records move only where carriers are. [H,q_v] = i g p_v Y_q exactly (both reviewers). The §5 and §6 readouts are energy or detuning profiles. A Record-probability footprint is energy profile x local carrier exposure (time-integrated <p_v>) x branch susceptibility, and it is exactly zero in carrier-free regions. The packet's channel set is static, so it cannot see history or imprint.

P5 (minor; §6): carriers enter kappa_D only by renormalizing chi_G: 1/chi_eff = 1/chi_G - lamJ^2 chi_p^stag. With chi_G = 0 they screen nothing (rho_ind = 0, and the carrier responds only at the source site). Chain check: chi = 1/4 and lamJ^2 chi_p = 2 give chi_eff = 1/2, V ratio 0.5000001, against 0.60962 = 9/8 - sqrt(17)/8 without carriers. The packet's 'not a Debye density' is correct, but this route is only implicit.
Non-problem (recorded): d = 2 + eta G is the correct native identity; the eta-free d = 2+G fails on B sites. Claims (1) and (4) need no correction.

missed_channels: (a) O(h^2) native pair-word to polarization vertex (P3a, exact coefficients). This is the lowest-order linear Record-polarization coupling; evaluate it before the h^6 ring channel. Status: computed (coefficient); the mediated range is open.

(b) Staggered Record-density channel. The direct degree vertex's linear response lives in the sublattice-odd Record density, which scalar shell readouts miss; an eta-weighted readout is required. Status: computed (structure).

(c) RCRS ring-energy vertex (native, missed as a link). By Hellmann-Feynman in ring-only ice dynamics, a Record's energy shift = (Delta c6/c6) x the ring energy of the 12 hexagons through it, which contains both electric and magnetic photon energy. RK-point flippability f(P) = 0.1753 - 3.86 P^2 (MC, L=6, statistical). A charged composite would give Q^2/r^4 and a neutral dipole r^-6, suppressed by Delta c6/c6 ~ 1e-6 at the tuple. Status: open (needs Coulomb phase, K_E, exposure).

(d) Magnetic, dual and fluctuation sector, conditional on c_pin. If the accepted c_pin(v,f) has the opposite sign to c_ring on the hexagons through v, the carrier's sign pattern is not a Z2 coboundary (periodic diamond, exact). The carrier then carries background pi-flux defects of the emergent U(1), with algebraic magnetic tails in a Coulomb phase. A magnitude-only change gives a neutral permeability impurity. Independently, (c_pin - c_ring) and Delta c6 interact through photon zero-point fluctuations (Casimir type): r^-7 at T=0 and r^-6 classically. This is algebraic, not Debye-screened in the transverse sector, and screened only by thermal monopoles. The packet evaluates only electric G charge. Test: sign of c_pin - c_ring. Status: open; requires a deconfined photon.

(e) History and imprint with native loop geometry. [H,q_v] = i g p_v Y_q, so the Record field is an integrated memory of carrier occupation, and a moving source leaves a trail. With n_e-gated hopping at h=0, a carrier is confined to its occupied ice loop. Loops are extended and Brownian: at L=10, 92% of sites lie on loops of length >= 512, and the local dimension is 1.95 at arc window 2048 (MC, statistical). Exposure density therefore goes as r^-1.05, out to a sqrt(arc reach). Possible cutoffs: ring reconnection at rate ~ h^6 c6/U^5, 1D localization by Record disorder, Bind backreaction, and the energy budget (0126 H2 bound, not reviewed here). Status: open.

(f) O(Q^2) smooth scalar degree response under complement breaking, proportional to cheap minus expensive defect populations and distinct from the packet's E^2 vertex. Polarized or sublattice-imbalanced backgrounds restore a linear, anisotropic r^-2 term. Whether S1 has such a background is a P49 question. Status: open.

(g) Birth as a mediated channel (graph surgery near matter: 2E_I contact, new length-4 cycles). A single anchored Birth is a finite local stiffness defect with dipolar or Casimir fall-off. The exception is a change to cycle space or connectivity (the N2 Born graph has 2 components; the union stays connected), which alters the global Gauss rank and flux sectors: global, but not a radial law. Status: open.

(h) Composite charged-defect binding: correctly OPEN in the packet. It is now sharpened by P2, which shows a kinetic bound excitation exists and that ground-state presence requires binding greater than ~2U_d.
